acceptance.output_evidence: Positioning is served by the /api/general/* behaviour, whose cache policy is opal-api-general-5min-cache (ce00305d): HeaderBehavior=none, QueryStringBehavior=none, DefaultTTL=300. X-FIRM-ID IS NOT IN THE CACHE KEY. Observed response headers on the authenticated fetch: 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300', 'X-Cache: Miss from cloudfront' -- a PUBLICLY cacheable, 300s, firm-agnostic entry for a bearer-authenticated artifact. THE CORRECT POLICY EXISTS AND IS APPLIED ELSEWHERE: opal-scoped-advisor-by-firm (45eb7514) has HeaderBehavior=whitelist ['X-Firm-Id'] and QueryString whitelist ['firm'], and is bound to the /api/scoped/advisor-intelligence/{artifacts,entities,*.json} S3 behaviours -- not to the path Positioning uses. All /api/scoped/* APIGateway behaviours use Managed-CachingDisabled (TTL 0). QUALIFICATION THAT MATTERS FOR THE REMEDY: with ONE unscoped artifact, adding firm to the cache key merely partitions identical bytes into per-firm entries. The cache key is downstream of the real defect, and fixing it alone would produce a correct-looking control over an unchanged exposure.

mutant.description: THE MUTANT THAT MATTERS IS ON AC2, because AC2 is the only PASS whose whole content is that an input is IGNORED -- and an assertion that an input is ignored passes trivially against an instrument that ignores everything. MUTATION APPLIED: vary the request URI while holding the bearer fixed, against the same scoped 403 envelope that reports the resolved firm. If the envelope were a constant string, the mutation changes nothing and AC2's 5 forgery arms prove nothing. FULL CONTROL SET CARRIED FORWARD: (1) authentication negative controls, DISTINCT: No bearer -> HTTP 401 51 B 'Missing or invalid Authorization header'. Bogus bearer -> HTTP 401 36 B 'Invalid or expired token'. Two different refusals, so the 200 on the valid bearer is a real authorization outcome and not a permissive endpoint. | (2) forgery oracle dynamism (the control that makes AC2 mean anything): The scoped 403 envelope echoes both the resolved firmId and the rewritten uri. Varying the request URI produced 3 distinct echoed uri values, proving the envelope is constructed per request. Without this, the constant 'cottonwood' across 5 forgery arms would be indistinguishable from a hardcoded string. | (3) discarded non-control, recorded: The first forgery test (forged X-Firm-Id against /api/general/) returned byte-identical 200s -- a result BOTH hypotheses predict, since that path ignores firm entirely. It could not discriminate and was discarded rather than reported as a pass. | (4) owned-paths instrument, exercised with 3 arms: 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Y passes on infra/aws terraform paths (rc=0) and is REFUSED on portal/, CLAUDE.md and a CTO deliverable (rc=1, 3 of 4) -- so the tool can refuse this serial. 0.4.0_DE_ClientPlatform~Y and 0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform~L both rc=1 VIOLATION on the identical two infra paths -- so the permission is discriminating, not vacuous. | (5) origin sweep completeness: list-objects-v2 over opal-data-portal-v2 returned 4,125 keys with terminal IsTruncated: None. No --max-items, no head, no client-side truncation. The 'zero firm-segmented positioning keys' verdict is over the whole bucket, not a page. | (6) origin label resolved against the world: The CloudFront origin ID reads S3-opal-data-portal-v2-json; listing that name returns NoSuchBucket. The real DomainName is opal-data-portal-v2.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. A code/config literal was not taken as evidence of what exists.
mutant.expected: Varying the URI changes the echoed uri field; if it does not, the envelope is a constant and AC2 is unsupported.
mutant.observed: FIRED. Three URIs produced three distinct echoed values -- /gold/artifacts/advisor_summary.json, /gold/artifacts/zzz_control_probe.json, /gold/entities/xyz/abc.json -- so the envelope is built per request and the constant firmId=cottonwood across 5 forged headers is a real resolution. NAMED LIMIT, NOT PAPERED OVER: the mutant fired on the URI FIELD, not on the FIRM FIELD. I never observed the firm field take a value other than cottonwood, because only one credential was obtainable. So AC2 rests on: a dynamic envelope (controlled), 5 ignored forgeries (exercised), and an unconditional overwrite at auth-validator-edge:388 running at viewer-request (source + applied). The strictly stronger control -- a second firm's bearer showing the field move -- was not run and its absence is stated rather than implied.
